name: Trichambaram Temple
deity: Krishna (in raudra form after the slaying of Kamsa)
builtDisplay: 15th–16th c. carvings and murals; attested 11th c.
significance: A Krishna temple at Taliparamba in north Kerala whose sanctum preserves carvings and murals of the 15th and 16th centuries, with the shrine already named in an 11th-century Sanskrit text. Its tank shrine to Durga is counted among the 108 ancient Durga temples of Kerala.

name: Valiyasala Mahadeva Temple
significance: One of the old Trimurti temples of Thiruvananthapuram, standing on the site historically associated with Kanthaloor Sala, a celebrated centre of learning in early Kerala.
story: Local tradition holds that temples to Brahma, Venkata Perumal and Mahadeva arose at the spots where queens of the Chera, Chola and Pandya kings performed sati after their husbands died in the Kanthaloor country.

name: Vaigalnathar Temple
builtDisplay: Early Chola (attributed to Kochengannan); century unrecorded
significance: A Shiva temple in the Kaveri delta held to be one of the three principal shrines raised by the early Chola king Kochengannan, and praised in the Tamil Saiva canon.

name: Sukutesvara Temple
significance: A living Shiva temple in the old town of Bhubaneswar behind the Lingaraja market, built of dry laterite masonry in the Kalinga pidha deul form and dated by its navagraha panel and structure to the 16th century.
story: Local tradition attributes the shrine to the heyday of the Kesari rulers.

name: Hridayaleeswarar Temple
significance: A Shiva temple at Thirunindravur west of Chennai, credited to Pallava builders of the 6th century and built in the Dravidian manner.

name: Vrindavan Chandrodaya Mandir
significance: An ISKCON temple under construction at Vrindavan whose foundation stone was laid in 2014 and which, at a planned 210 m and 75 floors, is intended to be the tallest religious monument in the world.

name: Kuzhanthai Velappar Temple
deity: Murugan (Kuzhanthai Velappar, as a young recluse)
style: Early Chera; South Indian, east-facing sanctum without a tower
significance: A hill Murugan temple above Poombarai in the Palani range, attributed to a Chera king of the early centuries CE; its image is nightly anointed with sandalwood paste that devotees receive as a medicinal balm.
story: The image is said to have been made by the siddha Bogar from navapashanam, an amalgam of nine poisons, and the temple's name recalls a poet-sage whom the god rescued by appearing to him as a child.

name: Vasudevapuram Temple, Tavanur
deity: Krishna (youthful form holding butter in both hands)
significance: A Krishna temple on the southern bank of the Bharathapuzha at Tavanur, one of a group of old shrines there that includes a Shiva and a Brahma temple and faces Thirunavaya across the river.
story: The child Krishna is said to have appeared to the saint Vilwamangalam Swamiyar here, and the image of the youthful Krishna was installed after the saint left his body.

name: Lalita Gauri Mandir
significance: A Shakta shrine near Kashi Vishwanath built in the first years of the 19th century by the exiled Nepali king Rana Bahadur Shah; the Ganga ghat beside it takes its name from the temple.

name: Kambatta Viswanathar Temple
significance: One of the twelve Shiva temples of Kumbakonam associated with the twelve-yearly Mahamaham festival; its name records a Chola-period mint that struck gold and silver coins on the spot.
